note: The base product guard's backend half (fe-country-split-plan §4.8, code-data-config-plan §2, S3), read by CountryWordsTest: no file in its scope names one of these words, a Danish locale chosen in a template or a Danish or Faroese place name, unless an entry of `allowed` permits that word or pattern in that file, with its reason: on every line of the file, or, when the entry gives a `text`, only on a line that holds that text (literally); an entry that has to stay file-wide says why in its reason. The rule (C5's): each file decoded as strict UTF-8 (a file that does not decode fails the test, unless its type is a binary one: png, jpg, jpeg, gif, ico, webp, pdf, zip, jar, class, ttf, otf, woff, woff2), normalised to NFC, line by line; the leading block comment skipped, and after it a comment line (one starting with *, /*, //, #, --, <!-- or <#--) with `Copyright` (the licence header), while a data line with the word is read; the `strip` patterns removed from the line; then each word, matched case-insensitively with a word boundary before it and none after (so `Søfart` matches `Søfartsstyrelsens`, and `DMA` matches neither `landmark` nor `scheduledMail`), and each pattern, with a word boundary before it; one finding per line, however many hits it holds. An entry that permits nothing fails, so the list shrinks with the code. Scope: niord-base's `niord/bootstrap/**` and `niord/src/main/**`, and niord-app's `niord-app/src/main/**` (paths relative to `be/`). Out of scope: `niord/sample/**`, which is Danish sample content (R11), and `niord/src/test/**`, which is test data and the IT fixture; this file stays outside the scope, because it names every word. C5's categories that permit nothing today have no entry: V001's comment, the S-62 'DK00' example, the country-repository link and Danish as a language hold no word. Neither 'EfS A' nor the 56/11 map centre is a word or pattern hit, and both stay. From 2026-11-03 the base English value is the neutral 'NtM Almanac', which is no hit either; the map centre stays.
